sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Container build and start steps
sections.what: Builds the OCR service image: installs Tesseract and its libraries, installs Python packages, copies the app, sets a non-admin user, and starts the server on port 8000.
sections.why: Likely reason: a repeatable package for running the service anywhere. Reason for each system package is only partly stated.
sections.watch_out: Because the language data is fixed at build time, changing the language setting alone does not add a language.

summary: Build recipe that packages the OCR service with the Tesseract text reader and the image libraries it needs, and runs it as a non-admin user.
purpose: Lets the OCR service run on any machine that can run containers, with its system tools installed.
why: Likely reason: the image needs Tesseract and image libraries that come from the operating system package manager. A comment in the file says this.
how: Starts from a slim Python 3.12 image. Installs Tesseract, English language data, image libraries, and build tools through the system package manager, then clears the package lists. Installs the Python libraries, copies the app, creates a non-root user, and starts the server with two workers on port 8000.
inputs: The requirements file and the app folder.
outputs: A container image that serves the OCR API.
risks: Build tools stay in the final image, which enlarges it and widens what an attacker could use. Only English language data is installed, so other configured languages will not work. The requirements file is not visible here.
debug: If the build fails at the system package step, check the package names against the base image. If OCR returns nothing, confirm Tesseract runs inside the container and the language data is present.
